title: Over 1 million people have clicked LinkedIn’s AI slop button
slides: One million clicked LinkedIn's AI slop button—why?
The button suggests 'repost' with AI-generated praise.
But few admit they used it, unlike this data.
Your feed now rewards fake engagement over real insight.
Next post: ignore the button, write your own take.
thread_text:
1. Why the button?

One million clicked LinkedIn's AI slop button, yet almost nobody admits it.

2. The hidden praise

The button auto-generates compliments like 'Great insights!' to boost reposts.

3. The silent majority

Data shows clicks, but users deny—creating a culture of fake engagement.

4. The feed's new law

Algorithms now reward AI flattery over genuine thought, burying real insight.

5. Ignore the button

Next time you see it, write your own take. Test it—your feed will thank you.

instagram.caption:
A million people clicked LinkedIn’s “repost with AI praise” button—yet almost none of them will say they did.  

The button silently generates flattery like “Great insights!” and attaches it to your repost. The click data is there, but the admissions aren’t.  

Your feed is now rewarding that fake engagement over actual thought—so real commentary sinks lower.  

If you create or post content, this is the new metric: flattery outperforms insight.  

Next time the button pops up, will you type your own take—or let the algorithm praise for you? 🙂
